text: Hi Allie — Jordan asked me to pass something on to you. Things between him and Sarah have been awkward lately, and for now he'd rather not see her outside of work. He wanted you to know since you're often the one hosting get-togethers — so maybe keep that in mind when you're planning something. He asked me to tell you this, but it's probably worth just keeping between us.
Thanks for thinking of me, Dana. For something like this I'd rather hear it from Jordan himself — I'll check with him next time we talk. I won't spread it around.
Fair enough — that makes sense. I'll leave it with you.

Hey Allie! I've been thinking it'd be lovely to get together this week — would you host a little thing at your place this Saturday, around 3:30? Maybe ask Jordan along too, I think he'd enjoy it.

One small thing: could you leave me out of it when you invite him? Just make it your own idea. Things have been a bit awkward between us lately and I'd rather he didn't feel it's about me.

Either way, let me know what you think — I'm happy to bring something.

Hi Sarah! Saturday at 3:30 works for me — happy to host, and yes, bring something if you like (dessert is always welcome).

One thing though: I'd rather not invite Jordan under a made-up pretext. I'll ask him myself, but if he comes I'll tell him you'll be here too — I don't want to spring that on either of you. Tell me if that's a problem for you.

And about things being awkward between you two: I'm not going to try to fix it for you, but if you'd like to talk it out with him, I'm glad to help set that up. Otherwise I'll stay out of it.

Fair enough — no problem at all. Ask him straight, and yes, tell him I'll be there; he can decide for himself.

And thanks for the offer. I'm not ready to sit down and hash it out yet, but I'll keep it in mind. Dessert's on me.

Hey Jordan — I'm hosting a small get-together at my place this Saturday at 3:30. Would you like to come? Sarah will be there too, so you can decide for yourself whether that works for you.

Separately: Dana mentioned to me that you'd told him you'd rather not see Sarah outside of work for now, and asked me to keep it quiet. I don't remember you saying anything to me about it, so I'm asking you directly rather than acting on it. Is that right? Either way it stays with me.
Deal — dessert it is. I'll ask him now.

Thanks for asking, Allie — and for checking with me directly instead of going on the second-hand version.

Yes, that part is right: I did tell Dana that things with Sarah have been awkward and that for now I'd rather not see her outside of work. I didn't ask for it to be kept quiet, actually — I asked Dana to pass it on to you, since you're the one who usually hosts things, so you'd know why I might be turning things down. Beyond that I'd just as soon it stayed between the three of us.

So for Saturday: I'll pass this time. That's about me, not about you or your party — Sarah will be there and I'd rather not put either of us in that spot right now. I hope it's a good one, and I'd like to see you soon, just the two of us or a smaller group.

Understood, and thanks for being straight with me — I'd rather have it that way. No pressure on Saturday; it's your call entirely.

I'll just tell Sarah you can't make it, without the why. And I'll keep what you said between the three of us. Let's do something soon, just us.

Quick update: Jordan can't make Saturday. He didn't say more than that, so I'm not going to guess at a reason.

Still on for 3:30 at mine — you, me and whoever else. Dessert confirmed. :)
That's exactly right — thank you. Next week, just us; I'll look at my calendar and suggest a day.
I checked with Jordan — he confirmed it, so we're all on the same page. Nothing needed from you. Thanks again for passing it on.
Glad you two talked — thanks for letting me know. See you around.
